paper.title: Regret Bound Balancing and Elimination for Model Selection in Bandits and RL

settings.name_in_paper: Model selection among base learners in stochastic contextual decision making (i.i.d. contexts)
unmapped: Model selection: a master algorithm chooses among M base learners each coming with a candidate regret bound R_i(n) that may or may not hold; regret compared with the best well-specified candidate bound
The learner knows (observes) the candidate regret bounds R_i(n_i(t)) of all base learners
At least one base learner is well-specified
settings.definition_quote: At each round $t$, a context $x_t \in \Xcal$ is drawn i.i.d. from some distribution, the learner observes this context, picks a policy $\pi_t \in \Pi$, thereby playing action $a_t = \pi_t(x_t) \in \Acal$, and receives an associated {\em reward} $r_t \in [0,1]$ drawn from some fixed distribution $\Dcal_{a_t, x_t}$ ... Each base learner $i$ comes with a \emph{candidate} regret (upper) bound $\regretbound_i \colon \NN \rightarrow \RR_+$

settings.name_in_paper: Model selection for stochastic linear bandits with adversarial contexts (nested dimensions, OFUL base learners)
unmapped: Nested model classes: only the first d_star (unknown) coordinates of theta_star are nonzero; base learners use dimensions d_i = 2^i
Base learners use per-learner norm bounds L_i, S_i known to them
settings.definition_quote: We consider the problem of linear bandits and are given $M$ instances of OFUL as base learners. Each instance $i$ considers only on the first $d_i = 2^i$ dimensions of the actions ... we here consider the setting where contexts $x_t$ (corresponding to the action set $\Acal_t$ at round $t$) are generated adversarially.
